title: On the geometry of the second Lagrange spectra
summary: The Lagrange spectrum $L$ is the set of finite values of the best approximation constants $k(α)=\limsup_{|p|,|q|\to \infty}|q(qα-p)|^{-1}$, where $α\in \mathbb{R}\setminus \mathbb{Q}$. It is a classical result that the pairs $(p,q)$ attaining these approximation constants arise from the convergents $(p_n,q_n)$ of the continued fraction of $α$. Consequently, $k(α)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}|q_n(q_nα-p_n)|^{-1}$. Moreira proved that the function $d(t)=HD(L\cap(-\infty,t))$ where $HD$ denotes Hausdorff dimension, is continuous.
